episode_summary: Dan, Andrew, and James host a Little Fish mailbag sharing listener-submitted curios: Pakistan’s CLCOT makes World Cup footballs (and bagpipes), London, Ontario’s many London lookalikes, a Dublin pub shut for holes in its walls, and chalk made of quadrillions of microscopic skeletons—plus tangents on cruise-ship newspapers, odd IMDb credits, Rubik’s cube feats, and a Nathan Fillion pavilion.

facts.fact: And CLCOT manufactures all the balls used in the World Cup. So Pakistan is always represented at the tournament even though the men's team is ranked 198th in the world.
London Ontario is a town of about half a million people between Toronto and Detroit in a bit of Canada sticking down between the Great Lakes.
The hole in the wall, pub and Dublin, was recently issued a closure order because there were holes in the wall.
And it turned out that according to John's calculations, there was roughly one between one and five quadrillion skeletons.
